svg.title: iOS · Resume blending? (launch offer over Projects) · portrait
svg.desc: Signed off by Steven 2026-09-30 (with the paused glyph grey rather than amber — the 2026-09-26 status scheme keeps amber for things in motion) and implemented the same day; verified against the running app on the iPhone 16 Pro Simulator (iOS 18.6) and the Mac with LL_OPEN=latest LL_AUTO=process LL_BLEND_PAUSE_AT=<0…1> (paused), a background/foreground round trip (resumed), a kill and relaunch (the offer), Resume Later (the card) and LL_BLEND_CANT_RESUME=1 (the Start Again card). ONE CHANGE FROM THE SIGNED-OFF DRAWING: the buttons read Resume · Discard · Later. Drawn Resume · Later · Discard with Later a plain button, iOS added a Cancel of its own as a fourth button (the 18.6 Simulator, 2026-09-30) — and dismissing through it would have raised the offer straight back — so Later carries the cancel role, which iOS always puts last. Parked (Later, or Resume Later on Processing), a job is never offered at launch again: the offer is only for the job the last close interrupted, and only one job ever runs, so there is never more than one. The launch offer for a blend the app was closed on (the blend engine saves the finished pieces of a clip as it goes, so an interrupted job can pick up where it stopped): a SwiftUI .alert raised from the app's root (App/LetsLapseApp.swift) over whatever tab is showing — Projects here, projects.portrait.svg (App/ProjectsView.swift) under the alert's 20 % black dim, its first card renamed to the offer's project so the set reads as one sequence; nothing else under it changes. Title 'Resume blending?'; message '“Sunset over Vltava” was 34% blended when LetsLapse closed. It picks up where it stopped.' — the project's display title and the job's whole-run percentage, wrapped as CoreText breaks it at 260 pt. Three buttons, in this order: Resume — opens Processing on that project, continuing from 34 % (processing.portrait.svg; the finished pieces are not blended again); Later — a plain Button, deliberately NOT role .cancel, which UIKit would move to the bottom under Discard — leaves the job on the project, where its card offers it again (project-detail.video.blend-paused.portrait.svg); Discard (role .destructive) — throws away the pieces blended so far; the project and its original are untouched. THE RULE: the offer appears once per launch, and only when an interrupted blend exists. If the app opened straight into the camera at launch, the offer waits until the camera closes, so shooting is never blocked. THE ALERT is the system's iOS 26/27 alert, drawn to the metrics measured on the iPhone 17 Pro Simulator on 2026-09-25 (project-photo.viewer.preview.prompt.portrait.svg) rather than the pre-iOS 26 270 pt card with hairline-separated buttons: a light glass card 320 pt wide centred on the safe area — 304 pt tall here, with a one-line title, three message lines and three buttons — radius ≈ 34, the text 30 pt in and left-aligned; the title 17 pt semibold black; the message 15 pt on 20 pt lines, #5F5F61 over the glass; the buttons stacked as 48 pt capsules 8 pt apart and 16 pt in, black 15 % over the glass, labels 17 pt medium. TINT: LL.accent #C36A00, not system blue — the app tints its alerts: the root view carries .tint(LL.accent) (App/LetsLapseApp.swift) and the asset catalog's AccentColor is the same #C36A00, which is what the measured alert shows. So Resume and Later are accent and Discard is system red #FF3B30. iOS 26 draws no alert action bold (measured), so Resume leads by its place on top, not by its weight. The status bar is not dimmed.
